extracted.intended_audience: Universities and equivalent research institutions preparing proposals for DFG Research Training Group funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for establishing and funding Research Training Groups (structured doctoral programmes) supported by the German Research Foundation (DFG). Covers eligibility, proposal content, funding, international variants, deadlines, and decision-making bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotion of graduated Early Career Researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Training Groups are established to promote early career researchers, with key emphasis on the qualification of doctoral researchers within a focused research programme and a structured training strategy. The aim is to prepare doctoral researchers for the complexities of the job market in science and academia and to encourage early scientific independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities and equivalent institutions with the right to award doctorates as well as universities of applied sciences that have an independent right to award doctorates or which, in cooperation with institutions that have been granted the right to award doctorates, can lead doctoral candidates to a doctorate in the subjects relevant to the Research Training Group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be institutions entitled to award doctorates (or cooperate with such institutions). This defines which organisations may submit establishment proposals and receive funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research programme — high scientific quality and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Research programme - high scientific quality and originality (interdisciplinary approach desired) at an international level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must present a research programme of high scientific standard and originality. Interdisciplinary approaches are welcomed. The programme should be positioned at an international level (i.e., competitive and relevant beyond the national context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification programme — relevance and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualification programme - of direct relevance to the research programme, including innovative teaching and supervision elements, which should clearly extend beyond the courses (doctoral colloquia) usually offered in doctorate programmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The training/qualification component must be tightly linked to the research programme and offer innovative teaching and supervision that go beyond standard doctoral colloquia. Emphasis on structured supervision and novel qualification measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visiting researcher programme (integration and internationalisation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visiting researcher programme - integrated into the qualification programme, adding internationalisation to the training provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must include a visiting researcher programme as part of the qualification measures to enhance international exposure and collaboration. This is intended to broaden doctoral researchers’ international experience and networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary approach (desirability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Training Groups with an interdisciplinary approach are warmly welcomed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not mandatory, interdisciplinary design is explicitly encouraged and considered favorable in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type and extent of funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Posts for doctoral researchers and postdocs. Funds for visiting researchers, research students, travel, workshops, small equipment, consumables, coordination, miscellaneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The programme funds personnel positions (doctoral researchers and postdocs) and operational items including visiting researcher support, travel, workshops, small equipment, consumables, coordination costs, and other miscellaneous expenses. Proposals should budget appropriately for these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Period and duration rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding Period - Up to nine years. In the case of Research Training Groups whose establishment proposal was decided on in November 2021, one funding period lasts four and a half years. For Research Training Groups whose establishment proposal is decided on in May 2022 or later, the first funding period is five years and the second funding period is four years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard maximum funding is nine years, but the structure of funding periods varies by decision date (specific transitional arrangements for proposals decided Nov 2021 and May 2022 onward). Proposers should plan project timelines and renewal expectations according to these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme Variation – International Research Training Groups (dual structure and mobility)
rubrics_metrics.description: In International Research Training Groups, a group of researchers at a German university and a group at a partner institution abroad assume joint responsibility for the structured research and qualification programme of the doctoral researchers. The programmes are developed collaboratively and involve dual supervision. Doctoral researchers in the participating groups are expected to spend at least six months abroad at the respective partner institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International RTGs require formal collaboration and joint responsibility between the German institution and an overseas partner, including dual supervision arrangements and an expectation of significant mobility (minimum six months abroad per doctoral researcher). Proposals must describe the partnership and mobility arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Deadlines and submission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft proposals may be submitted at any time; Establishment proposals – following consultation with the DFG’s Head Office – may also be submitted at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no fixed cut-off dates for draft proposals or (after prior consultation) for establishment proposals; proposers should consult the DFG Head Office before submitting establishment proposals. Procedural consultation with the Head Office is a prerequisite for establishment submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and Guidelines requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You can find all the necessary forms for this program in the overview of forms and guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use the DFG’s prescribed forms and adhere to the programme’s guidelines (links provided). Ensure all required documentation and forms from the DFG overview are completed and included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making body — Senate Committee on Research Training Groups (role)
rubrics_metrics.description: This Senate Committee is responsible for advising the DFG’s decision-making bodies on issues relating to Research Training Groups, for giving the final recommendation for draft proposals and for preparing the final decisions by the relevant Grants Committee. The members of this Senate Committee also serve as the academic and scientific members of the DFG Grants Committee on Research Training Groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding the Senate Committee’s advisory and recommendation role is important for proposers: draft proposals receive final recommendation from this committee before Grants Committee decisions. Membership overlaps with the Grants Committee’s scientific membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making body — Grants Committee on Research Training Groups (responsibility and composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Grants Committee on Research Training Groups is responsible for the establishment and funding of Research Training Groups. The committee is made up of 39 scientists and academics elected by the DFG's Senate from all research areas, and two representatives of the federal government (Bund) and one representative from each of the 16 federal states (Länder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final establishment and funding decisions are made by this committee. Proposers should be aware of the committee’s broad disciplinary membership and the presence of governmental representatives; meeting dates are published.
